Padding K removes the FP8 GEMM tail bottleneck

Padding K removes the FP8 GEMM tail bottleneck
Memory summary

The agent traced the previous benchmark’s severe slowdown on K=4127 to masked loads in the GEMM loop. It revised the Triton solution to pad K to a multiple of the tile size and choose tile configurations based on shape. The new benchmark passed with a geometric-mean peak fraction of 0.1314, up from 0.0397.

Relevant prior context

The first Triton FP8 GEMM had already passed correctness, including numeric-stress cases. Its benchmark showed that K=4127 took 11.254 ms and achieved only 12.305 TFLOPS, while the skinny-M case achieved 55.843 TFLOPS. The agent identified tail masking and low parallelism on skinny M as performance issues.

Important non-obvious context

The task uses genuine FP8 e4m3 tensor-core multiplication with FP32 accumulation, applies per-output-channel weight scaling, and returns bf16. The solution must preserve the reference Model, get_inputs, and get_init_inputs interface and register weight and weight_scale buffers for state-dict loading. torch._scaled_mm and torch.ops.aten._scaled_mm are forbidden.

The environment had CUDA 13.0 and an NVIDIA B200 (SM 10.0). Searching found a nvidia_cutlass_dsl Python package, but no CUTLASS headers in /usr/local/cuda/include; the agent chose to improve Triton instead.

Recording summary

The agent began by comparing against the previous run: K=4127 had collapsed to 12 TFLOPS because each loop iteration used masked loads, and M=32 had too few blocks to use the GPU well. It considered padding K, split-K, autotuning, and CUTLASS. The CUTLASS search found Python DSL files under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/nvidia_cutlass_dsl, but the CUDA include directory had no CUTLASS headers.

The solution change (+32 -22) introduced _round_up and _choose_config. For M≤64, it selected (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) = (32, 128, 128) when N≥8192, otherwise (32, 64, 128), with 4 warps and 3 stages. Larger shapes used (128, 256, 128), with 8 warps and 3 stages. If K was not divisible by BLOCK_K, the code padded both activation and weight along K before launching the Triton kernel:

K_PAD = _round_up(K, BLOCK_K)
if K_PAD != K:
    a = torch.nn.functional.pad(a, (0, K_PAD - K))
    b = torch.nn.functional.pad(b, (0, K_PAD - K))

For K=4127 and BLOCK_K=128, this pads to 4224, allowing the loop to run without a partial K tile. The code retained FP32 accumulation, applied the channel scale, and stored bf16 output.
